faq.a: Jealousy comes when you want what someone else has, or worry that you are missing out or less special. It is a normal feeling that everyone has sometimes.

faq.q: Is it bad to feel jealous?
faq.a: The feeling is not bad; it is just a signal. What matters is what you do. Being unkind because of jealousy hurts people, but naming it and talking about it helps.
asks: Am I a bad friend for being jealous?

faq.q: How do I stop feeling jealous?
faq.a: Name the feeling, take a breath, and think about your own good things. Try saying something kind to the other person. Talking to a grown-up you trust helps too.
asks: How do I get over jealousy?

faq.q: What is the difference between jealousy and envy?
faq.a: Envy is wanting what someone else has. Jealousy is often worrying that you will lose someone or something to another person. In everyday talk, people use both words for the same feeling.
asks: Are envy and jealousy the same?

faq.q: What if I feel jealous of my brother or sister?
faq.a: That is very common, especially when a new baby arrives or one child gets lots of attention. Tell a parent or carer how you feel and ask for some special time together.
asks: Why am I jealous of my sister?

facts: The phrase "green-eyed monster" for jealousy comes from Shakespeare's play Othello, written around 1603.
In a 2002 study, babies just six months old looked upset when their mother gave attention to a lifelike baby doll.
